proposals.before: When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Works.
proposals.after: When Yougui acceded, he made the Emperor custodian of the Eastern Capital, acting prefect of Kaifeng, and honorary Minister of Education (Situ).
proposals.reason: Chinese 檢校司徒 is honorary Minister of Education/Situ, not Works (司空); the idiomatic gloss wrongly repeats Works from the prior unit.

proposals.before: On gengwu Ma Chuo, Zhendong deputy and Two Zhes commander, became Honorary Grand Mentor and co-counselor, took Xiongwu at Qinzhou, and was made Marquis of the Opening State.
proposals.after: On gengwu Ma Chuo, Zhendong deputy and Two Zhes commander, became Honorary Grand Mentor and co-counselor, took Xiongwu at Qinzhou, and was made Marquis of the Opening of the State.
proposals.reason: Chinese 開國候 is a scribal/variant for 開國侯 (Marquis of the Opening of the State); idiomatic already conveys the title but 'Opening State' is slightly opaque—minor clarity fix.

proposals.before: On dingchou Yu Jing, acting minister of works and grand counselor, became vice minister of works, then was exiled to Luzhou as marshal for nepotism toward officers.
proposals.after: On dingchou Yu Jing, acting minister of works and grand counselor, became vice minister of works, then was demoted to Laizhou as marshal for nepotism toward officers.
proposals.reason: Chinese 萊州司馬 is Laizhou, not Luzhou; also 眨 is demotion/exile wording—correct the place name.

proposals.before: On gengwu in the twelfth month Prince of Fu Youzhang, former Yunzhou commissioner, became Xuzhou commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: On gengwu in the twelfth month Prince of Fu Youzhang, former Yunzhou commissioner, became Xuzhou (Xu prefecture) commissioner and Honorary Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu prefecture; idiomatic 'Xuzhou' risks confusion with 徐州—clarify.

proposals.before: The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xuzhou; Yin refused replacement; an edict stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Youzhang, Niucunjie, Liu Yan, and others against him.
proposals.after: The court had posted Prince of Fu Youzhang at Xuzhou; Yin refused replacement; an edict stripped his titles, restored the surname Jiang, and sent Youzhang, Niu Cunjie, Liu Yan, and others against him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 牛存節 is Niu Cunjie; idiomatic fuses the name as Niucunjie.

proposals.before: Cang and Wei are subordinate; Zhang Jun is commissioner of Xiang."
proposals.after: Chan and Wei are subordinate; Zhang Jun is commissioner of Xiang."
proposals.reason: Chinese 澶州 is Chan/Chanzhou, not Cang; correct the prefecture name.
Chinese 牛存節 is Niu Cunjie; idiomatic fuses the surname and given name.

proposals.before: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: That first month Xuanyi commissioner Prince of Guangde Jing Quanyu died.)〉
proposals.after: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: That first month Xuanyi commissioner and Prince Guangdejing Quanyu died.)〉
proposals.reason: Chinese 廣德靖王 is a posthumous compound title for Quanyu; clarify the English gloss.

proposals.before: (《New History of the Tang: Basic Annals》: In the ninth month of year two Jin took Beizhou; defender Zhang Yuande died.
proposals.after: (《New History of the Five Dynasties: Basic Annals》: In the ninth month of year two Jin took Beizhou; defender Zhang Yuande died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 歐陽史 refers to Ouyang Xiu's Xin Wudai Shi (New History of the Five Dynasties), not the Tang history.

decisions.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education in this translation's office system, whereas Minister of Works corresponds to 司空.
Marquis of the Opening State is the established rendering used elsewhere in the chapter corpus. The proposed 'Opening of the State' is not clearer and does not correct a semantic error.
萊州 is Laizhou, not Luzhou. The proposal corrects the place while preserving the demotion described by the sentence.
Xuzhou is the normal romanized form of 許州 in this corpus. The proposed parenthetical repeats the same name without resolving the shared pronunciation with 徐州.
牛存節 is the personal name Niu Cunjie. The existing English accidentally fuses surname and given name.
澶州 is Chan Prefecture. Cang would correspond to 滄 and is the wrong place.
This is another fused rendering of 牛存節 and should use the same Niu Cunjie form as the earlier sentence.

decisions.after: (Zizhi Tongjian: In the first month of the second year, Quanyu, Xuanwu military commissioner, acting director of the Secretariat, and Prince Jing of Guangde, died.)〉
decisions.reason: 廣德靖王 is Quanyu's posthumous title, Prince Jing of Guangde. The revision also restores 守中書令 and corrects 宣武 from the existing Xuanyi mistranscription.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宣武節度使、守中書令、廣德靖王全昱卒

decisions.reason: 歐陽史 here is Ouyang Xiu's New History of the Five Dynasties. Calling it a Tang history identifies the cited source incorrectly.

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair separates the surname and given name in 牛存節; the chapter-wide personal-name claim must use the same corrected English form.
The second local person record for 牛存節 must not retain the fused English name after the accepted repair.
The reviewed sentence separates Quanyu's personal name from 廣德靖王, his posthumous princely title. The structured claim should do the same.
